{{Nihongo|'''Hiroshi Amano'''|天野 浩|Amano Hiroshi|born September 11, 1960}} is a Japanese [[electrical engineer]] specializing in the field of [[semiconductor]] technology. He is a co-inventor of the blue [[LED]], for which he was awarded the 2014 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] along with [[Isamu Akasaki]] and [[Shuji Nakamura]].<ref name="Nobel Prize">{{Cite web|title=Nobel Prize in Physics 2014|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2014/summary/|url-status=live|publisher=NobelPrize.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240407181951/https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2014/summary/|archive-date=2024-04-07|access-date=2014-10-07}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Hiroshi Amano was born on September 11, 1960, in [[Hamamatsu]], [[Shizuoka Prefecture]], Japan, the son of father Tatsuji and mother Yoshiko.<ref name="Nobel bio">{{Cite web|title=Hiroshi Amano – Biographical|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2014/amano/biographical/|url-status=live|publisher=NobelPrize.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260110075807/https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2014/amano/biographical/|archive-date=2026-01-10|access-date=2026-02-07}}</ref>

In 1979, Amano entered [[Nagoya University]] as a student of the Department of Electrical Engineering,<ref name="Nobel bio"/> graduating with a [[Bachelor of Engineering]] in 1983. He then went to the Graduate School of Engineering, where he received a [[Master of Engineering]] in 1985 and a [[Doctor of Engineering]] in 1989.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hiroshi Amano|url=https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/hiroshi-amano/|publisher=Cornell University|access-date=October 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name=nagoya>{{Cite web|title=Hiroshi Amano|url=https://en.nagoya-u.ac.jp/research/distinguished-faculty/hiroshi_amano/|url-status=live|publisher=Nagoya University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215021458/https://en.nagoya-u.ac.jp/research/distinguished-faculty/hiroshi_amano/|archive-date=2025-12-15|access-date=2026-02-07}}</ref>

In 1988, Amano became a research associate in the School of Engineering at Nagoya University. From 1992 to 2010, he was an assistant professor, associate professor, and a professor in the Faculty of Science and Technology at [[Meijo University]]. In 2010, Amano returned to Nagoya University, where he is currently a professor in the Graduate School of Engineering.<ref name=nagoya/> He has been director of the Akasaki Research Center since 2011.<ref name="Nobel bio"/>

== Research ==
[[File:Blue light emitting diodes over a proto-board.jpg|thumb|Blue [[light-emitting diode]]s]]

Amano joined Professor [[Isamu Akasaki]]'s group in 1982 as an undergraduate student. Since then, he has been doing research on the growth, characterization, and device applications of group-III-[[nitride]] semiconductors, which are well known as materials used in blue [[light-emitting diode]]s (LEDs) today. In 1985, he developed low-temperature deposited buffer layers for the growth of group-III-nitride semiconductor films on a sapphire substrate, which led to the realization of group-III-nitride semiconductor-based LEDs and [[laser diode]]s. In 1989, he succeeded in growing p-type [[Gallium nitride|GaN]] and fabricating a p-n-junction-type GaN-based UV/blue LED for the first time in the world.<ref name="Nobel bio"/>

Known to be keen on research, Amano's laboratory was always lit late at night, such as weekdays, holidays, New Year's Day, and was called "no night castle".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://getnews.jp/archives/680824|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141015194805/http://getnews.jp/archives/680824|title=快挙の師弟、笑顔で握手＝「今も緊張」天野さん―赤崎さん、不夜城紹介・ノーベル賞 ｜ ガジェット通信|archive-date=October 15, 2014}}</ref> According to his students in the laboratory, Amano has an optimistic and temperate personality, and is never angry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/shizuoka/20141009/CK2014100902000094.html|title=「天野浩さんの人柄を仲間が紹介」|access-date=October 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141011155853/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/shizuoka/20141009/CK2014100902000094.html|archive-date=October 11, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/region/news/141009/rgn1410090081-n1.html|title=ノーベル物理学賞受賞の天野浩教授 研究に没頭「とにかく熱心」 静岡|first=SANKEI DIGITAL|last=INC|website=産経ニュース|date=October 9, 2014 }}</ref>

== Family ==
Amano's wife was a Japanese lecturer at [[Comenius University]] in Bratislava, Slovakia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Nobel Prize winner explains the use of LED lights |url=https://uniba.sk/detail-aktuality/back_to_page/aktuality-1/article/a-nobel-prize-winner-explains-the-use-of-led-lights/ |access-date=2023-11-15 |publisher=Comenius University |language=sk-SK}}</ref>
